newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-FRENTZEN EMERGES FROM SCHUMACHER'S SHADOW.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FRENTZEN EMERGES FROM SCHUMACHER'S SHADOW.

text.p: San Marino Grand Prix winner Heinz-Harald Frentzen admitted he felt a little lost for words, but his smile said it all.
His victory was the sweetest day of his motor racing career, his maiden Formula One triumph and a perfect reply to the critics and rivals who doubted his credentials as a front-line driver.
"It is fantastic. A wonderful feeling," he said.
Frentzen did not say so, but it may have been extra satisfying for him to finish 1.2 seconds clear of his oldest rival and fellow German -- double world champion Michael Schumacher.
The pair grew up together, were rivals in karting and junior formulae in Germany and team mates in the junior Mercedes-Benz team. Frentzen's former girlfriend became Schumacher's wife.
But he did not talk about any of this. In his hour of greatest triumph, his first victory for Williams, Frentzen was modesty personified.

"I feel speechless," he said. "This is such a fantastic feeling. This is a hard track on the brakes and I was concerned about them after my experience in Melbourne (where a brake fault caused him to spin off).
"I didn't really push towards the end but tried to maintain a rhythm as I could see Michael coming up behind me in my mirrors. I wanted to hold him off and I was worried about rain.
"But that is not when I won the race. I won it when I saw Michael going into the pits and Jacques (Villeneuve) going in before me as well.
"I knew that was my moment to push, so I pushed to do the two quick laps which would gain me the time I wanted before I went in myself. I was concerned about the traffic, but it was just all right.
"The pit stop was quick. So, when I came out of the pits and saw 'P1' on my board the next time around, I could hardly believe it. I was so happy and so surprised as well to be in the lead."
As Frentzen talked, Schumacher added a few asides and jokes which added to the convivial atmosphere of the post-race news conference.
"Why?" said Schumacher, when Frentzen talked of keeping his rhythm and his concentration.
"Because now it is my time, my turn," said Frentzen, knowing that for once, and at last, he was the top dog, out of Schumacher's shadow and a winner.
Even in Italy, where Schumacher is admired as a great Ferrari driver, this was a popular victory by Frentzen. And one he fully deserved.
